description: Reverse-arg form of cp/mv/install via ``-t DIR`` or ``--target-directory=DIR`` placed the directory as a non-final positional. ``_CP_MV_RE`` parses ``cp SRC DST`` and treats the LAST positional as the write target; with ``-t DIR`` the directory comes BEFORE the source list, so the existing extractor captured a source path (probably outside the protected zone) instead of the protected destination. Before the fix, ``cp -t tools/cc/hooks/ /tmp/evil.py``, ``mv -t tools/cc/hooks/ /tmp/evil.py``, ``cp --target-directory=tools/cc/hooks/ /tmp/evil.py``, and ``install -t tools/cc/hooks/ /tmp/x`` all passed. Fix (2026-09-05): ``_target_directory_value`` reads the flag off the tokenizer's option view -- ``-t DIR``, glued ``-tDIR``, a cluster past ``t``, any unambiguous GNU abbreviation of ``--target-directory`` quoted or bare, ``=`` or space bound -- after consuming a value-taking flag's separated value; every positional is then a source landing under DIR. The regex it replaced captured the directory after a literal ``-t`` / ``--target-directory=`` and disagreed with the token-view predicate on a quoted flag.
